title: What segmentation is and why firms segment
summary: Segmentation divides a mixed group of customers into groups with similar needs. It benefits customers and the organization.

chunks.heading: What market segmentation is
chunks.explanation_md:
**Market segmentation** divides a market into **well-defined slices**. A **market segment** is a group of consumers who share a similar set of **needs or profile characteristics**.

Another way to say it: dividing a group of **heterogeneous** customers with different needs into **homogeneous** subgroups or segments with similar needs and preferences.

Common types of segmentation: **demographic, geographic, behavioral and psychographic**.

chunks.heading: Examples: Uber options and special fares
chunks.explanation_md:
Two examples of serving different groups with different offers:

- **Uber**: Uber Go (affordable compact rides), Uber XL (comfortable SUVs), Uber Go Priority (priority pickup), Uber Premier (comfortable sedans) and Moto Connect (to send packages only).
- A **travel booking page** with special fares: Regular, Student, Senior Citizen (up to Rs 600 off), Armed Forces (up to Rs 600 off) and Doctor and Nurses (up to Rs 600 off).
chunks.exam_line: Examples: Uber Go, XL, Go Priority, Premier, Moto Connect; special fares for students, senior citizens, armed forces, doctors and nurses.

chunks.heading: Why segment the market?
chunks.explanation_md:
**Benefits to customers:** tailored products and services, customized solutions, a relevant offering.

**Benefits to organizations:** identification of unfulfilled needs, better product design, more targeted promotions, increased customer satisfaction.
chunks.exam_line: Customers get tailored products, customized solutions, relevant offerings. Organizations get unfulfilled needs identified, better design, targeted promotions, higher satisfaction.

questions.stem: Explain market segmentation with the Uber ride options and the special fares on a travel booking page.
questions.model_answer_md:
**Market segmentation** divides a market into well-defined slices: groups of consumers with similar needs. Customers with different needs become homogeneous subgroups.

**Uber.** Different options serve different needs: Uber Go (affordable compact rides), Uber XL (comfortable SUVs), Uber Go Priority (priority pickup), Uber Premier (comfortable sedans) and Moto Connect (to send packages only).

**Travel booking page.** Special fares are offered to Student, Senior Citizen (up to Rs 600 off), Armed Forces (up to Rs 600 off) and Doctor and Nurses (up to Rs 600 off), besides Regular fares.

These show offers tailored to groups of customers. Segmentation benefits customers with tailored products and relevant offerings, and benefits the organization through better product design and more targeted promotions.

**Conclusion.** Both examples show one firm serving several groups with different offers.
